object_description: multi-part two-storey volume with a backbone and offset wings
design_condition: The building's main volume runs parallel to the highway as a noise-protective backbone, while offset volumes settle into the landslide topography and frame differentiated outdoor spaces around the slope and rock formation.

positive.statement: The figure of several building parts reacts convincingly to the unsettled topography caused by the landslide.
The main volume provides noise protection for the outdoor spaces behind it.
The volumes engage with the slope edge and striking rock formation, creating an interaction with the morphology of the place.
The landscaped right of way leads through a park-like green space to the covered access situation.
The formation of the building structure connects differentiated and well-oriented open spaces with the interior organization.
The two-storey volume sits relatively reservedly in the landscape and organizes the school facilities in a child-friendly manner.
The shifted sections make corridors narrow and expand in interesting ways, providing clear views of the surrounding landscape.
The upper level is well ventilated away from the noise, while the lower rooms are protected by the existing earth wall.
The pent roof brings additional light into the depth of the rooms and breaks up the volume.
The project blends unobtrusively yet spectacularly into the landscape, with a sufficiently strong building expression.
Low volume requirements, a simple support system and minor topographic interventions enable economical implementation.

negative.statement: The entrance is somewhat set back and cramped within the terrain formation.
The proposed disposition of the two kindergarten rooms cannot be combined.
The reception is somewhat decentralized and cannot be found immediately from the main entrance.
The wheelchair-accessible ramps are very long, so the access theme is overused and requires a lot of space.
The separation of vertical access for fire safety reasons would be difficult and complex, and additional emergency exits are required.
The relatively high level of building development has a negative impact on operation and gray energy.
The proposed insulation for the ground-floor overhang is not sufficient for the MINERGIE-P standard.
The wet cells are only partially grouped, and unresolved technology shafts will reduce usable areas.
